content:
The iPhone Ultra will make its debut next month, and the latest leaks suggest that the front-facing camera on this device may be positioned in an unusual spot.

The two front-facing cameras on the iPhone Ultra may both be placed in a corner position rather than centred.

When the iPhone Ultra arrives, it will be Apple's first attempt at a foldable iPhone. As a result, this device will differ from the design of a "normal" iPhone in several ways — and the cameras are one of them.

The iPhone Ultra is said to come with two rear cameras — a main lens and an ultrawide — plus two front-facing cameras.

The reason it has two front-facing cameras is that a foldable device will have two screens: one on the outside, and a larger screen that only appears when unfolded.

Up to now, we've been expecting the front camera on the outer screen to be centred. But according to the latest leak, the camera's position may be far more unconventional.

A third-party screen protector circulating online appears to show a cut-out for a camera in the top-right corner of the outer screen and one in the top-left corner of an inner screen.

It's quite possible this accessory maker simply got it wrong. Like everyone else, they're just guessing. But if this leak turns out to be true, it would mark a significant departure from previous front-camera placements.

Apple has always placed the front-facing camera in the top centre of the iPhone. Moving it to a corner could mean that in many selfies — especially group photos — users end up looking at the wrong lens.

As for the camera on the inner screen, not having it centred actually makes more sense, since the camera cannot be placed on the fold, and selfies are more likely to be taken using the outer screen anyway. But if even the outer-screen camera isn't centred, users may need some time to readjust.

If Apple moves the iPhone Ultra's front-facing cameras to a corner, do you think it would be a problem? Let us know in the comments section.
